diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3 V, datasheet reading 3.3 V
diffs.evidence: The second reading copied the module's single nominal value (MSP0961 user manual: "Operating Voltage 3.3V", "The IPS display module can only be connected to 3.3V"; it gives no min/max) into both vmin and vmax. The part models a 3.3 V supply with a tolerance band of 3.0-3.6 V. The board has no regulator, so VCC goes straight to the ST7735S. The ST7735S V1.1 datasheet DC characteristics give VDD operating voltage 2.5 V min (2.75 typ, 4.8 max) and VDDI interface voltage 1.65 V min (1.8 typ, 3.7 max), so a 3.0 V minimum is inside the chip's rated range. The manual also says a bare screen's LEDA backlight runs at 3.0V-3.3V.

diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 3.6 V, datasheet reading 3.3 V
diffs.evidence: The 3.3 V in the second reading is the vendor's nominal value (MSP0961 manual: "VCC ... LCD power supply is positive (3.3V)"), not a stated maximum. The real limit is the chip, since VCC feeds VDD and VDDI directly. The ST7735S V1.1 datasheet gives "Interface Operation Voltage VDDI 1.65 1.8 3.7 V" (recommended max 3.7 V, absolute max 4.6 V) and VDD max 4.8 V. So 3.6 V, about 3.3 V +10%, stays under the tightest rated operating limit of 3.7 V. The part still tells users to supply 3.3 V and never 5 V.
